images.caption: Figure 1:Overview of our approach.(a,b) Packed trajectory canvas (PTC) generation reduces visual-quality drift compared with sequential rollout. (c) MTEdit offers more trajectories and turns than existing datasets. (d) Fine-tuning on MTEdit improves multi-turn editing performance in instruction following (IF), content consistency (CC), and visual-quality stability (DRS).

Figure 2:Overview of our data construction pipeline.(a) Seed image curation, which selects source images with high resolution and aesthetic quality; (b) PTC generation, in which VLMs derive a PTC prompt from each source image to guide closed-source image models in generating the corresponding PTC; and (c) PTC to multi-turn conversion, which processes the generated canvases into multi-turn editing trajectories with turn-level instructions and target images.
Figure 3:Statistics of MTEdit.(a) Edit-type taxonomy, (b) multi-turn data distribution, and (c) instruction word cloud.
Figure 4:Qualitative results on the step-wise sub-bench.Our method achieves competitive editing performance and maintains visual quality without noticeable degradation across editing turns.

Figure 5:Visual quality comparison at Turn 8.From left to right: the source image and outputs from models trained on data from PTC generation and sequential rollout. Enlarged crops show fewer artifacts and cleaner details with our pipeline.
Figure 6:Block causal attention and 3D interleaved RoPE for Qwen-Image-MTEdit.Image and text tokens are temporally interleaved as “[Image] - [Text] - [Image] - ...”.
Figure 7:Example of PTC generation used in the MTEdit construction pipeline.

Figure 8:Visual quality drift comparison.We compare our data with rollout-style results generated using Seedream 5.0 Lite/GPT Image 2/Nano Banana 2. Columns show results at Turns 1/4/8. The visual quality of rollout-style methods degrades noticeably starting from Turn 4 (e.g., spurious speckling appears on the ground near the car), whereas our results remain relatively stable.
Figure 9:Qualitative results on the persistent-constraint sub-bench.Yellow boxeshighlight representative editing errors.
Figure 10:Qualitative results for textual-reference multi-turn image editing.Red boxeshighlight representative editing errors.
Figure 11:Qualitative results on the short-instruction sub-bench.Later turns progressively lengthen the flower stems using concise, context-dependent instructions.
Figure 12:Representative examples from MTEdit.Rows show step-wise, persistent-constraint, textual-reference, and short-instruction editing trajectories.
Figure 13:Failure case of PTC generation.Content from different panels may interfere with one another, requiring additional filtering during data construction.
